title: Mosaic contract slate — per-contract GPU reservation proposal
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet proposes a per-contract reservation allocation called 'Mosaic' — a compact mapping of each Dedicated contract to a regional pool, reserved GPU SKUs, burst entitlement, and utilization envelope. Aim: reduce per-token jitter by pairing contracts with consistent region+sku slates while retaining cross-contract fairness for burst windows.

Executive summary (short):
- We propose allocating reservations at the granularity of (contract, region, sku-family) instead of global slabs.
- Each reservation has: committed GPUs, burst buffer (short-term), a utilization target band (steady / peak), and a primary fallback model variant when capacity saturates.
- Assumed target uplift: improve SLA fulfillment from 94.1% -> 97.3% for tiered contracts while keeping fleet-wide utilization > 75% by enabling controlled bursting and quick re-routing.

Key assumptions:
- Reservation units are counted in vGPU-equivalents (1 vGPU ≈ 80% of a p100-like slot for our mixed fleet).
- Average peak length per request spike: 70s (used to size burst windows).
- Target long-term operating utilization (steady band): 65—80% per slab, with bursts to 100% for up to 12 minutes per hour for high-priority contracts.
- Cross-region penalty for failover estimated as +18% tail latency; only allowed when necessary.

Reservation matrix (preview):
ContractID | Customer (alias) | Region | GPU SKU family | Reserved (vGPU) | Burst buffer (vGPU) | Start | End | Util target | Notes
C-2047 | BlueHarbor | us-west1 | A100-80GB | 48 | 12 | 2027-07-01 | 2029-06-30 | 70% steady / 95% peak | primary for low-latency customers; cache warmup policy enabled
C-1993 | Ledgerly | eu-west1 | H100-80GB | 24 | 6 | 2027-07-15 | 2028-07-14 | 60% steady / 90% peak | prefers dedicated KV-cache lanes (no sharing)
C-2088 | Shopline | us-central1 | A100-80GB | 32 | 8 | 2027-08-01 | 2028-08-01 | 68% steady / 96% peak | auto-fallback to quantized variant if latency > 300ms
C-2110 | NovaHealth | europe-west3 | A100-40GB | 16 | 4 | 2027-07-01 | 2029-01-01 | 60% steady / 92% peak | compliance-controlled region; KMS bound
C-2155 | AtlasML | asia-southeast1 | H100-80GB | 20 | 5 | 2027-09-01 | 2028-09-01 | 65% steady / 94% peak | early-burst tranche for go-live (first 30d)

Notes on fields:
- Reserved: baseline committed capacity (billing/commit).
- Burst buffer: ephemeral additional vGPUs allowed sourced from a regional burst pool; amortized across contracts by weighted fair share.
- Util target: the suggested steady utilization band; we use it to trigger autoscale or redistribute slice assignments.

Utilization scenarios (short forecast, 12-month rolling):
- Conservative: assume 5% demand growth, maintain burst credit monthly; fleet utilization ~74% (safe).
- Base (expected): 12% demand growth, dynamic burst used 30% of hours; fleet utilization ~80% with SLA > 97%.
- Aggressive: 28% demand growth, burst usage 55% of hours; risk of regional saturation pushes tail latency > SLA.

Operational policies embedded in Mosaic: 
1) Priority ordering: (critical contracts) -> (standard reserved) -> (best-effort). Critical contracts can preempt bursts after 10m of sustained high demand.
2) Burst credit refill: per-contract monthly replenishment seeded from unused committed hours; unused burst credits expire quarterly.
3) Fallback routing: when region-level available vGPU < 10% of demand for a contract, route to nearest compatible region with +failover-penalty tag; notify customer and open incident if crossover persists > 15m.
4) Quantized variants: customers can opt-in to quantized model fallbacks to maintain throughput; billing differentiation applied when fallback used.

Sample short table: projected monthly committed vs expected consumption (C-2047 BlueHarbor)
Month | Reserved | Expected avg consumption | Expected peak hours | Burst used (vGPU-hr)
Jul-2027 | 48 | 35.2 | 22 | 720
Aug-2027 | 48 | 37.8 | 28 | 1,060
Sep-2027 | 48 | 41.0 | 42 | 1,880

Contingency plans (if region saturation triggered):
- T+0: Enable cross-contract burst cap at 60% of regional burst pool to prevent single-customer starvation.
- T+5m: Auto-scale equivalents in adjacent region (if available) and initiate cache warmup on fallback region.
- T+15m: Trigger operations runbook for triage; if sustained > 30m, consider temporary throttling of non-critical contracts and engage customer success for impacted accounts.

Cost/commitment impact (example calculation):
- Committed vGPU cost (baseline): $X per vGPU-month (placeholder — finance will fill in).
- Burst cost: 2.1x of committed per vGPU-hr during burst windows to incentivize commitments.
- Billing note: when fallback quantized variant is used, bill at 0.7x token rate but record quality-regression metric.

Open questions (items to resolve before finalization):
- precise vGPU-equivalence mapping for new H100 variants (ask hardware team for final conversion table).
- regional burst pool sizing policy (currently heuristic; needs simulation).
- legal review for cross-region failovers for compliance customers (esp. NovaHealth).

Next steps and owners: 
- run a 30-day simulation against July production traces to validate burst pool sizing (owner: Diego Alvarez) — due 2027-07-18
- finalize pricing multipliers for burst and quantized fallback with finance (owner: Maya Patel) — due 2027-07-22
- produce customer-facing one-pager describing Mosaic reservation behavior (owner: Soraya Mendes, customer-success) — due 2027-07-29

Appendix: quick glossary
- Reserved: baseline committed capacity tied to contract and billing.
- Burst buffer: ephemeral capacity pulled from a shared pool; not guaranteed beyond short windows.
- vGPU-equivalent: normalized compute unit across heterogeneous GPU SKUs.
- Quantized variant: model configured with lower precision/latency-cost profile for fallback.

This document is an iterative working sheet — add rows to the reservation matrix below as new contracts on-board. Use the linked simulation ticket (JIRA-ENG-4128) for trace inputs and reference for the final sizing rules.
